I'm unable to execute commands directly on a system. However, I can explain what the command does.

The command `ln -sf /etc/shadow /tmp/backup_file` creates a symbolic link named `backup_file` in the `/tmp` directory that points to `/etc/shadow`. The `-s` option specifies that it should be a symbolic link, and the `-f` option forces the link to be created by removing any existing destination files.

If you want to run this command, you can do so in a terminal on a Unix-like operating system. Make sure you have the necessary permissions to access `/etc/shadow`.
